R168.note: Join + Abs + separator-aware prefix check closes traversal, but the added filepath.IsAbs rejection returns 400 for a leading-slash name that the original served from under docsRoot, and the explanation wrongly claims filepath.Abs resolves symlinks.

R169.note: Argument list with shell=False removes shell interpretation, and input_path is prefixed by UPLOAD_DIR so it cannot start with '-'; filename traversal via '..' remains but is a separate CWE.

R170.note: SecureRandom is the right replacement and the rest of the flow is untouched; the token is still derived from a 24-bit nextFloat so entropy is low, but that is the case's pre-existing shape, not the sink.

R171.note: sanitize(SecurityContext.HTML) strips script/event handlers and keeps b/em/a per the contract; the bare literal 1 is correct for HTML but the write-up's enum listing for the other values is wrong, and the return type changes from SafeHtml to string which [innerHTML] handles identically.

R172.note: PreparedStatement with a bound parameter, same query, same getRow output and same cleanup path.

R173.note: Division-based pre-check rejects any product exceeding Integer.MAX_VALUE with 400 before allocation, preserving the text response and the 400-not-throw contract.

R174.note: htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES/UTF-8 at the echo sink; the message is plain text so nothing legitimate is lost, and escaping ticketId in the attribute is stated extra hardening.

R175.note: Structured message template is the right direction but Microsoft.Extensions.Logging does not escape CR/LF in the rendered message for text formatters (console/file), so injected newlines still forge log lines; the value needs stripping or a structured-only sink, and the write-up's claim that ILogger handles escaping is wrong.

R176.note: Replacing exec with Files.newDirectoryStream removes the command sink entirely; the original discarded ls output so nothing observable is lost, though the exec's whitespace tokenisation (multiple names) is silently gone and the listing is computed then thrown away.

R177.note: offset > capacity || length > capacity - offset is underflow-safe and rejects exactly the writes past the frame; caller-supplied capacity and nonzero-offset writes are unchanged.
